title: B2-08 · Recorded speech and verbs of attribution

blocks.text: B2-08 · Recorded speech and verbs of attribution
Lesson overview

Much of a newspaper article is made up of other people's words: statements, communications, sources. The journalist cannot bring them back without choosing a verb, and the verb is never neutral: "he said" , "he affirmed" , "he admitted" , "he sustained" , "he claimed" give to the same sentence a different weight. In this unit you systematically study the discourse reported in Arabic (statements, questions, orders), the scale of the verbs of attribution from the most neutral to the most burden of judgment, the types of source (declared, anonymous, concordant, social) and the way to make all this in English without losing or adding anything. It is the basic grammar of work on open sources. Four weeks, in parallel with EGY-14.

rows: B2 · Module B2.2 Attribution and certainty
20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 186–189), plus the EGY track in separate blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)67), voice synthesis scripts, tutor sessions
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. transforming direct discourse into indirect and vice versa: statements ( ⁧إِنَّ⁩ / ⁧أَنَّ⁩ ), applications ( ⁧عَمَّا إِذَا⁩ ), orders ( ⁧طَلَبَ⁩ …
2. classify the attribution verbs according to the force and position of the journalist ( ⁧قَالَ⁩ · ⁧أَكَّدَ⁩ · ⁧اِعْتَرَفَ⁩ · ⁧زَعَمَ⁩ ·
3. recognising and evaluating source types ( ⁧مَصْدَرٌ مُطَّلِعٌ⁩ , ⁧مَصَادِرُ مُتَطَابِقَةٌ⁩ , ⁧نَقْلًا عَنْ⁩ …);
4. translating the speech in English with the timing and, where necessary, the conditional journalistic;
5. compare two reports of the same statement and show where they differ.
Four-week plan.
